current_findings: SQLite remains canonical; earlier equal-information storage comparison did not establish answer-quality superiority for another engine.

Structured content retains exact source/citation/review bindings and stable learner ownership, with local integer remapping. Divergent mutable content remains an explicit conflict, not automatic convergence.
Schema42 pins local and remote replica instances and local node names, persists body-free offers and scoped recipient interest, and commits received content with its data receipt in one transaction.
Lost acceptance/data responses recover from durable records. Historical data receipts do not assert current body existence; replay cannot recreate a permanently retired source.

Permanent controls route only through recorded peer/object boundaries. Still-configured peers with empty current allowed scopes can reconcile those IDs without receiving new bodies; removed or replaced peers remain unresolved.
A new pending deletion between compaction and receipt writing was reproduced against the pre-review function. The corrected receipt transaction checks pending work and refuses completion until retry.

All five individual artifact types remain retired after a later permitted content transfer. Retiring one artifact is not claimed to erase every independently retained conversation representation; the public forget CLI operates on a whole session.

Six Meta/Qwen/Mistral responses informed Stage34 design/review. The coordinator retained durable acceptance despite objections, fixed the demonstrated race, and documented rejected claims. No unanimous approval is claimed.

Actual SSH/coordinator, quarantine reconciliation, complete hot/full propagation/consumers and managed restore remain open. Legacy protected transport stays refused; full sync remains explicitly false.
Unknown legacy delivery/scope history is not inferred or broadcast. Envelope bounds do not bound cumulative retained ledger history. No owner DB/config/hooks/archives or live peer was changed.

Schema43 records local native-evidence capture and exact committed peer row contributions in the same transaction as bodies/receipt. Accepted offers create no contribution. Local-origin history is excluded from scoped content packets.

Existing rows without matching history remain explicitly unattributed after their first new peer receipt. Changed body versions and replaced database instances cannot borrow prior facts. Integer learner remapping binds receipts to actual receiver rows.
A->B plus A->C->B demonstrates that two delivering peers do not prove independent upstream origins. Retention authorization remains not_evaluated; native recapture is not regrant.

Initial Stage35 suspected learner deletion defect was a reversed dependency assumption: observation depends on record. Corrected test preserves the independent project record; no reverse purge trigger was added.

Corrected design and result councils returned Meta/Qwen/Mistral. Existing entry-point peer validation refuted an asserted sender-injection path; a direct helper current-instance/peer check and negative test were nevertheless added.
Schema44 uses ordered peer/scope permission generations and separate denial history. Receiver withdrawal includes lost-acceptance inbound offers; stale receipts never recreate bodies.

Bounded rollback tracing observes the actual canonical purge under one writer transaction. Exclusive matching peer history permits eviction; ambiguous retention stays hidden with explicitly incomplete cleanup.
Regrant alone leaves known IDs awaiting fresh content. Exact new-offer coverage rejects receiver-only retained extras and rolls back release/content/receipt together. Permanent retirement still wins.
Reproduced whole-transaction abort cleanup defect fixed: do not open a new mode-reset transaction or mask the original error with missing temp-table/savepoint cleanup.

Installed lesson exposed public forgetting incorrectly blocked by quarantine. Scoped metadata-only retirement selection now permits explicit forgetting without authorizing body reads; wrong-scope and deep learner checks pass.

Three-provider result council raised concurrency objections; concrete second-connection, process-exit, generation, FK and bounds tests plus SQLite documentation were used to arbitrate. No unanimous approval or arbitrary-schema guarantee claimed.
